author: reek
body: The system catalog stores metadata about all tables, columns, and indexes in the database. It is the single source of truth for schema information. DDL operations (create table, create index, drop table) mutate the catalog.

author: reek
body: Update and delete by RowId. The catalog had neither, which is why IssueStore called a catalog-delete-row that has never existed: a field update was written as delete-then-insert because there was no way to say update.

author: reek
body: Both go through heap-delete and then hand the row to catalog-insert-row rather than to heap-insert, so validation and index maintenance stay in one place instead of being repeated here.

author: reek
body: What they do NOT do is retract the old row's index entries. catalog-update-indexes only ever adds, and nothing in this chapter removes an index key, so an index still points at the RowId the row used to occupy. That gap predates these two functions -- there was no delete of any kind before them -- and it is why they are honest about being row-store operations with index maintenance that only grows. Fixing it means an index-delete path, which is its own change.
